name: Gin Rummy
summary:
Gin Rummy is a two-player card game in which each side tries to organise a ten-card hand into combinations while keeping the value of leftover cards low. It uses a single standard 52-card deck without jokers and has no narrative setting. This version runs in a web browser on desktop and mobile and is published by NowPlay.

A hand begins with ten cards dealt to each player and one card turned face up to start the discard pile. On a turn, a player takes either the top card of the face-down stock or the visible top discard, then places one card face up on the discard pile. Valid combinations, called melds, are sets of three or four cards of equal rank and runs of three or more consecutive cards in one suit, with aces counting low. Unmelded cards form deadwood, valued at 1 for an ace, 10 for a face card and face value otherwise. A player whose deadwood is 10 or less may knock, ending the hand; the opponent then attaches eligible cards to the knocker's melds, and the side with less deadwood scores the difference. Knocking with no deadwood is gin, worth a 25-point bonus and immune to lay-offs, while a defender who matches or beats the knocker's count scores an undercut bonus of 25. A match ends at 100 points.

Turns are limited to 45 seconds. The game can be played alone against computer opponents or online against other people. A tutorial introduces the rules, a solo ladder moves from single hands to a full match, and a daily challenge is offered.
